paper.title_en: Hadron physics experiments with HypTPC at J-PARC
paper.abstract_en: We present an overview of hadron physics experiments performed with the Hyperon Spectrometer at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility, with particular emphasis on baryon spectroscopy using hadronic reactions. The Hyperon Spectrometer, centered on a large-acceptance time projection chamber (HypTPC), enables exclusive measurements with high statistics under high-intensity meson beams. Recent theoretical developments, including dynamical coupled-channels approaches and lattice QCD calculations, highlight the necessity of precise hadronic data, especially for the πN → ππN and πN → KY reactions, to extract nucleon resonance properties reliably. In this context, the J-PARC E45 experiment aims to provide high-precision measurements of these reactions over a wide kinematic range, addressing long-standing issues such as missing resonances and possible hybrid baryons. The current status of the HypTPC program and future prospects are also discussed.
